title: Apple Smart Glasses Leaked: Plans to Deeply Integrate Siri and Tap Into Third-Party App Ecosystem
excerpt: Apple is planning to deeply integrate the Siri AI agent into its in-development smart glasses product, aiming to use the App Store ecosystem advantage to challe
content_html:
Apple is planning to deeply integrate the Siri AI agent into its in-development smart glasses product, aiming to use the App Store ecosystem advantage to challenge Meta's Muse AI voice assistant and competitors such as Samsung and Google.

According to Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman, Apple's core strategy is to reuse the existing iPhone developer ecosystem. Software developers will not need to develop dedicated apps for this wearable device; instead, they will directly expose specific functions from existing apps for Siri to invoke. This means users will be able to smoothly complete complex tasks through voice commands in the future, such as hailing a ride via Uber, booking a restaurant with OpenTable, ordering at Starbucks, shopping on Amazon, and booking movie tickets through Fandango, all without opening or browsing the specific applications.

Currently, Meta's Muse has already gained a first-mover advantage in the smart glasses market, while Samsung and Google are also deepening cooperation with developers through the Android XR platform. However, with its massive mobile app ecosystem and mature API integration capabilities, Apple is trying to build a more pervasive hardware agent experience. Nevertheless, how to strike a balance between deep intelligence and increasingly severe privacy concerns will still determine whether it can truly win market recognition.

This strategic move marks that competition among tech giants in the AR and AI integration race has moved from pure hardware interaction to a deep contest over application ecosystems. Apple's attempt to break down hardware barriers through its existing ecosystem is expected to accelerate the evolution of consumer-grade AI glasses into all-scenario service agents.
